incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN customers (federal agencies and enterprises)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote attackers exploited a maximum-severity authentication bypass (CVE-2026-20182) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager to obtain administrative privileges; the activity overlaps with operational relay box infrastructure typically associated with Chinese state operators.
incidents.impact: CISA ordered all U.S. federal civilian agencies to patch by Sunday May 18, citing active exploitation. Talos tracks the lead actor as a sophisticated pre-positioning campaign on SD-WAN controllers — high-trust devices that sit in the middle of corporate east-west traffic — with additional separate clusters dropping XenShell, Godzilla and Behinder webshells using public proof-of-concept code.

incidents.vector: The Nitrogen ransomware group breached Foxconn's North American manufacturing environment using its standard double-extortion playbook (data theft followed by encryption on Windows/VMware servers).
incidents.impact: Production at Foxconn's North American factories — which assemble products for Apple, Intel, Google, Dell and Nvidia — was disrupted; the group claims it stole 8 TB / 11M files including confidential project drawings. Foxconn says affected factories are resuming normal production.

incidents.vector: An unidentified ransomware operator breached West's network on May 4, stole data and encrypted systems used to ship, receive and manufacture injectable drug-delivery components.
incidents.impact: West, a $3B/year supplier of stoppers, seals and components for injectable medicines used by major drug developers, disclosed the incident via SEC 8-K. Global business operations were temporarily disrupted; some sites have restored manufacturing, shipping and receiving but full restoration is incomplete. Unit 42 is leading the IR engagement.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party IT services provider and abused legitimately-deployed HPE Operations Agent/Manager tooling to execute VBScripts on the victim's web servers and domain controllers, then registered a malicious Windows network provider (mslogon.dll) and password filter to harvest cleartext credentials.
incidents.impact: Stealthy intrusion went undetected for approximately 123 days, during which the actor harvested credentials, established web-shell persistence on internet-facing servers, and moved laterally to highly sensitive assets. Microsoft IR engaged after detection; persistence and credential interception were reestablished post-detection before full containment.

incidents.victim: TanStack / npm ecosystem (incl. Mistral, UiPath, OpenAI)
incidents.vector: Operators compromised maintainer credentials for the TanStack React framework and pushed malicious package versions; the embedded Shai-Hulud worm self-propagated to ~400 dependent npm libraries and now wipes systems where owners try to revoke stolen tokens.
incidents.impact: Compromised packages included libraries from AI company Mistral and automation vendor UiPath. OpenAI confirmed two employees were impacted and is rotating code-signing certificates. The Shai-Hulud source code was subsequently leaked publicly with a $10K bounty for the largest follow-on supply-chain attack, virtually guaranteeing copycat campaigns.

incidents.vector: Threat actors published hundreds of malicious Ruby packages designed to execute cross-site-scripting attacks and steal data specifically from RubyGems engineering staff systems.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled all new user sign-ups while investigating. Unrelated to the concurrent TanStack/npm Shai-Hulud incident. What the attackers ultimately tried to steal from staff has not been publicly disclosed.

incidents.victim: Google Threat Intelligence Group disclosure — undisclosed open-source admin tool vendor
incidents.vector: GTIG identified a zero-day exploit developed with the help of AI (hallucinated CVSS score, textbook-Pythonic structure) targeting a 2FA bypass in a popular open-source web-based system administration tool.
incidents.impact: First confirmed case of AI-assisted zero-day weaponization by a criminal threat group preparing a mass-exploitation campaign. GTIG worked with the affected vendor to patch and disrupt before launch; the specific product and group were not named publicly.

incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas (9,000+ schools, universities and K-12 districts)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters compromised Instructure's environment via an issue in Canvas Free-for-Teacher accounts (after an earlier breach disclosed April 29), then defaced the Canvas login page with a public ransom demand on May 7 when Instructure declined to pay.
incidents.impact: Canvas — used by 41% of North American higher-ed institutions — was taken offline during final-exams week, forcing Baylor, UT, Penn, Iowa State, Duke, Oklahoma, Florida, Northwestern, Princeton, Ohio State and many K-12 districts to delay exams. 3.6 TB of data (names, emails, student IDs, messages) covering an estimated 275M users was stolen. Instructure paid the ransom; the group claims data was destroyed and provided shred logs.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers (User-ID Authentication Portal exposed)
incidents.vector: A buffer-overflow zero-day (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3) in the PAN-OS Captive Portal lets unauthenticated attackers achieve root remote code execution on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls via crafted packets; exploitation began April 9 and uses open-source tunneling tools (EarthWorm, ReverseSocks5) rather than custom malware.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 tracks the activity as CL-STA-1132 — likely state-sponsored, with EarthWorm tooling historically associated with Volt Typhoon and APT41-class actors. Post-exploitation: shellcode injection into nginx, Active Directory enumeration via firewall service-account credentials, systematic log destruction. Shadowserver found 5,800+ publicly exposed VM-Series firewalls. Initial fixes shipped May 13.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — code-signing certificate theft (China-linked tooling)
incidents.vector: An attacker posed as a customer and socially-engineered two DigiCert tech-support employees into running a malicious SCR (screensaver) file; one CrowdStrike EDR agent had been misconfigured and was not reporting to the central console, allowing nearly two weeks of undetected access.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole 27 EV code-signing certificates by exfiltrating initialization codes from in-flight certificate orders, then used them to sign Zhong Stealer payloads (a family associated with the Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog / APT-Q-27). All 60 certificates issued during the access window were revoked. Discovered after a third-party researcher reported the abuse.

incidents.vector: Threat actors with deep access to AVB Disc Soft's internal network shipped DAEMON Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate that contained a first-stage backdoor; a second-stage QUIC RAT payload was deployed only to selected high-value systems.
incidents.impact: Trojanized installers have been distributed since at least April 8. Kaspersky observed several thousand infections but second-stage deployment was limited to a dozen targeted government, scientific, manufacturing and retail systems in Russia, Belarus and Thailand. Tradecraft closely mirrors prior Chinese-APT software-vendor compromises (Notepad++, CCleaner).

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia and UK
incidents.vector: Voice phishing operators impersonating internal IT staff direct targets to passkey/SSO-themed lookalike portals; an adversary-in-the-middle flow proxies the legitimate SSO sign-in, captures session cookies and registers an attacker-controlled MFA device for persistence.
incidents.impact: Once authenticated, UNC6671 uses Python and PowerShell scripts against Microsoft Graph and SharePoint/OneDrive to programmatically exfiltrate millions of files, then extorts victims under the "BlackFile" brand — escalating with Gmail-spam floods, voicemail threats and swatting against C-suite personnel. Has previously co-opted the ShinyHunters brand for added pressure.

incidents.victim: Schemata (DOD contractor) — U.S. service members and military training data
incidents.vector: Schemata, an AI virtual-training platform serving the U.S. Department of Defense, exposed an unauthenticated API online that allowed direct access to military course data and service-member records.
incidents.impact: Per security firm Strix, the company took roughly 150 days to secure the leaky API after notification. The volume and sensitivity of records exposed has not been publicly quantified.

incidents.victim: Tens of thousands of users at 13,000+ organizations (mostly U.S., healthcare/finance/professional services/tech)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — credential theft / token compromise
incidents.vector: Polished "code of conduct" / disciplinary-action phishing emails sent April 14-16 carrying PDF lures that funnel users through two CAPTCHAs and intermediate "Paubox-encrypted" pages into an adversary-in-the-middle Microsoft sign-in flow that captures auth tokens, bypassing non-phishing-resistant MFA.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Research tracked 35,000+ targeted users across 26 countries. Successful AiTM compromises grant immediate session access to victim accounts, bypassing MFA. Healthcare (19%), financial services (18%) and professional services (11%) were the most-targeted verticals.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; attackers obtained access to Trellix's source-code repositories.
incidents.impact: Source code stolen from Trellix, one of Europol's closest cybersecurity partners. The company says no changes were made to its shipping products and that law enforcement was notified.

incidents.vector: A pro-Palestinian hacktivist group conducted sustained distributed-denial-of-service attacks against Canonical's web infrastructure and APIs.
incidents.impact: Ubuntu users were unable to install or update the OS during the multi-day attacks. The same group (313 Team) previously took down BlueSky and Mastodon and is now also subject of a class-action by Chime Financial customers over a separate DDoS event.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure and potentially its customer API-key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust told customers — including Cloudflare, Vercel and Stripe — to rotate API keys. The company provides AI observability tooling, so stolen keys could grant adjacent access to customer AI pipelines.

incidents.vector: An intruder maintained access to Best Western's reservation systems for over six months between October 2025 and April 2026; the initial-access mechanism has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Best Western is notifying guests of brands including Best Western, Sure Hotels and WorldHotels. Specific data categories accessed have not yet been published.

incidents.vector: Lapsus$ obtained Vodafone source code (initial access vector not disclosed) and leaked it publicly after the telco refused to pay the extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Source code from EU telco Vodafone published by Lapsus$. Material impact will depend on what was in the leaked repositories.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Skoda's German e-commerce platform.
incidents.impact: Skoda says customer data was likely accessed. The number of affected customers and specific data categories have not been published.
